business_scope.primary_industry_name: C-Suite Executive Search and Specialist Tech Headhunting

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Republic of South Africa (national unitary jurisdiction; all nine provinces governed by a single corporate law regime under the Companies Act 71 of 2008, with no sub-state incorporation variants)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid legal system: Roman-Dutch civil-law heritage overlaid with English common-law commercial doctrine, constitutional supremacy under the Constitution, 1996, and binding judicial precedent; corporate law is substantially English-derived but codified in national statutes.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: South Africa-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (2002, effective 2003)
South Africa-United States Double Taxation Convention (1998)
South Africa-People's Republic of China Double Taxation Agreement (2001)
SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment (2006)
African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Agreement (ratified by South Africa 2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Companies Act 71 of 2008, section 28(3) read with the Companies Regulations, 2011, as amended by the Companies Amendment Regulations, 2023 (mandatory Beneficial Ownership Register declaration and filing with CIPC); Prevention of Organised Crime Act 121 of 1998; Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004 (targeted financial sanctions); Financial Intelligence Centre Guidance Notes 1 and 7 (customer due diligence and politically exposed persons).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register is not publicly searchable; access restricted to CIPC, the Financial Intelligence Centre, the South African Revenue Service, the Companies Tribunal, and mandated law-enforcement and intelligence agencies; the company must maintain an internal beneficial-ownership record available for lawful inspection)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of each foreign director's passport bio-data page (FICA-compliant identity verification)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority or notary in the director's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the issuing state is party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention) or Consular Legalization at the South African embassy/consulate for non-Convention states; followed by certified English translation if the document is not in English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign director's proof of residential address (bank statement or municipal utility account, issued within 90 days of lodgment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating bank or municipal utility authority in the director's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable; sworn English translation required for non-English documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of each corporate shareholder (including supporting evidence of the ultimate beneficial-owner chain)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, ACRA, Delaware Division of Corporations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; certified English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Executed Consent to Act as Director (CIPC Form CoR 35.2) and FIC declaration, with notarial attestation if signed outside South Africa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Director executing before a notary public; notarial attestation in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if executed entirely outside South Africa

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing screening of all directors, shareholders, natural-person beneficial owners, and key principals against: (i) the FIC domestic politically exposed persons (PEP) list and corruption nexus database; (ii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) the targeted financial sanctions list adopted under POCDATARA 33 of 2004; (iv) the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists as a prudent benchmark for USD-denominated Retainer_Wire funding; and (v) international adverse-media and enforcement watchlists (including Interpol notices). Cross-border payment rails (Wise B2B and correspondent wire banks) will independently require UBO declarations, source-of-funds, and source-of-wealth evidence. The business is classified as Low_Risk_Standard under FICA, triggering standard customer due diligence with simplified ongoing monitoring; no mandatory independent external AML audit is required at this tier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Portal - Name Clearance and Company Registration module (https://eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All CIPC submissions, the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI), and supporting affidavits must be prepared in English. Company names may only contain Latin-alphabet characters; foreign-script names must be transliterated into phonetically equivalent English/Latin spelling. Numerals and limited punctuation (e.g., '&', '.', ',') are permitted; special characters, consecutive spaces, and suffixes implying a different legal form are prohibited. A private company name must end with 'Proprietary Limited' or the suffix '(Pty) Ltd'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: CIPC may extend a name reservation for one additional six-month period upon written application lodged before expiry; a lapsed reservation requires a new name-clearance filing with a fresh fee. Rejection appeal: within 10 business days of the CIPC refusal notice, the applicant or any aggrieved person may apply to the Companies Tribunal under section 160(2) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 using Form CTR 142, serving the application on CIPC and all affected persons; the Tribunal typically issues a ruling within 30-60 days. Practical alternative: refile with a more distinctive name, or incorporate without a reserved name (using the company registration number as the name) and apply for a name change post-incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with compliance conditions. Under section 23(1) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, the registered office must be a physical street address in South Africa (a post-office box is insufficient) and must be the location where the company's statutory records are kept and accessible. A licensed virtual-office or serviced-office provider may lawfully supply the registered office and accept legal process, provided the address is publicly recorded with CIPC and the underlying service agreement is maintained. For a low-risk executive search and headhunting business, virtual offices are widely accepted; however, financial institutions and payment-rail providers (including Wise B2B) may require supplementary proof of operational substance, such as a service agreement, dedicated telephone line, and director availability for due diligence calls.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for CIPC and FIC: estimated <5% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk professional services company with no cash-intensive operations. Elevated for the Department of Employment and Labour (DOEL), which supervises private employment agencies under the Employment Services Act 4 of 2014 and may conduct scheduled or unannounced compliance inspections of licensing, records, and fee practices; estimated 10-15% annual probability of a DOEL compliance visit.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per CIPC 2025 fee schedule (approx. R50 per beneficial ownership filing)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (approx. R700-R900 per month)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated professional tariff / prevailing market benchmark (approx. R1,800 for two notarial certificates)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization handling at DIRCO, Pretoria (two foreign-origin documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO), Legalisation and Apostille Section

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: FIC registration carries no statutory fee; external consultant fee is prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial screening database provider (e.g., World-Check/LexisNexis, Dow Jones Risk & Compliance)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Republic of South Africa Companies Act 71 of 2008 — ss 13 (incorporation), 14 (registration formalities), 19 (legal personality), 32 (companies register), 66 (board of directors), 69 (officers); Companies Regulations 2011.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), Republic of South Africa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1A)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; the company must allot and issue at least one share. No escrow account or capital deposit is required at incorporation for this jurisdiction.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation previously executed are ratified and adopted. 2. The ordinary shares are allotted and issued to the subscribers in accordance with the subscription register, fully paid or as otherwise recorded. 3. The registered office of the company is fixed at the address contained in the filed Notice of Incorporation. 4. The individuals named in the Officers' Schedule are appointed as directors and, where stated, company secretary, each consenting to act in terms of sections 66 and 69 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. 5. The directors are authorised to register the company for applicable licences and to open bank accounts. This resolution shall take effect upon the certificate of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the CIPC e-Services portal and submit Form CoR 9.1 with up to three proposed names in order of preference. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee by credit/debit card or electronic funds transfer. The name reservation remains valid for six months and can be renewed upon expiry.
required_dossiers: Completed CIPC Form CoR 9.1 (Application for Reservation of Name)
Identity document or passport of the applicant/subscriber
Proposed company name and any trading name details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, immediately file a fresh application with alternative names or apply for reconsideration within the statutory objection period; no refund of the name reservation fee is granted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Memorandum of Incorporation and Statutory Forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC pre-filing compliance desk / corporate law practitioner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation using Form CoR 15.1A, incorporating the share structure, directors' powers, quorum rules and adoption of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 default provisions. Prepare Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) and obtain signed subscriber consents on Form CoR 14.3, together with directors' and officers' consent-to-act forms.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1A)
Draft Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1)
Incorporation consents of subscribers (CoR 14.3)
Consent to act as director and officer forms
Share capital, share class and rights schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise the MOI to address any CIPC formal compliance objections and resubmit; non-mandatory clauses that are inconsistent with the Act are severable and will be flagged for amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the validated name reservation, final CoR 14.1, final CoR 15.1A, subscriber consents and director/officer consent forms into the CIPC BizPortal. Review the pre-filing summary, pay the applicable incorporation fee, and retain the CIPC transaction reference and acknowledgment receipt.
required_dossiers: Valid CIPC name reservation certificate
Final Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1)
Final Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1A)
CoR 14.3 subscriber consents
Director and officer consent to act forms
CIPC incorporation fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the filing is queried, correct the listed defects and resubmit within the CIPC rejection/prescription window; request an extension or administrative review where the objection concerns a factual record or duplicate filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and Establishment of Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC (certificate issuance) / First Board of Directors (share allotment)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the electronically stamped Certificate of Incorporation from the CIPC e-services account. Convene the board action to allot the subscribed shares to the initial shareholders, issue share certificates, and establish the statutory records including the share register, register of directors and register of prescribed officers.
required_dossiers: CIPC-generated Certificate of Incorporation
Issued share certificates
Register of shareholders (Companies Act s 50)
Register of directors and prescribed officers (Companies Act s 24)
Copy of the MOI and any company rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apply for a re-issued or corrected certificate by lodging Form CoR 17.1 with a supporting affidavit and prescribed fee; rectification of registers is executed by a board resolution with updated entries filed at CIPC where required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Governance, Bank Account Opening and Operational Licensing Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors / Department of Employment and Labour (DEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first formal board meeting to adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, appoint the auditor or accounting officer, set banking mandates, and authorise opening of corporate bank accounts. Simultaneously prepare the private employment agency registration dossier under the Employment Services Act 4 of 2014 for the executive search and headhunting business scope.
required_dossiers: First board resolution minutes and adoption record
List of appointed directors, company secretary and auditor/accounting officer
Bank mandate and account opening forms
Private employment agency registration application under the Employment Services Act 4 of 2014
Proof of registered office and physical premises details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any appointment or resolution is defective, reconvene the board to ratify retrospectively; where the DEL registration is delayed, obtain an acknowledgement of receipt and operate within the permitted exemption period pending issuance of the certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DEL) — Employment Services Directorate (private employment agency registry)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Registration as a Private Employment Agency (Employment Services Act 4 of 2014, s 20)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for standard office-based executive search and headhunting activity; Registration tier under the EIA Regulations 2014 (GN R327 Listing Notices 1-3) would only be triggered by physical development, land alteration or building expansion in a sensitive area.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source effluent; office wastewater must meet municipal sewer by-laws. Volatile organic compound (VOC) and refrigerant emissions are limited to conventional HVAC and cleaning-agent levels. General waste handling must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008, with separation of any hazardous office waste such as spent batteries and e-waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety inspection and fire compliance certificate; occupancy and structural safety clearance under the National Building Regulations; workplace clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 including risk assessment, first-aid provisions and emergency evacuation plans; civil defense registration with the district municipality where local by-laws so require.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); portal: SARS eFiling at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity deriving South African-source income or carrying on a South African enterprise must apply to SARS for registration as a taxpayer and obtain a SARS income tax reference number. Applications are lodged electronically through the SARS eFiling portal for non-resident companies using Form IT100/Company Registration; proof of foreign incorporation, local public officer appointment, physical address, and financial year-end are required. VAT registration is obtained separately via SARS VAT 101 if taxable supplies exceed the threshold; the same tax reference number is used for income tax, VAT, PAYE, and customs purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (a South African resident private company is taxed as a separate entity on worldwide income under the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962; no pass-through treatment is available for a (Pty) Ltd; territorial exceptions apply only through specific reliefs such as the participation exemption and controlled foreign company rules)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not have a US-style check-the-box election. Elections available include: headquarter company status under section 9I for a foreign-owned South African company; asset-for-share rollover elections under section 42; hybrid mismatch ordering and corresponding elections under sections 25O-25U; and grouping/assessment elections for controlled foreign companies under section 9D. All elections are made through SARS eFiling or prescribed forms and must be supported by contemporaneous documentation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, as amended; administered by SARS)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration: ZAR 1,000,000 in taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary VAT registration: ZAR 50,000 in taxable supplies in the past 12 months; non-resident electronic service providers may have separate deemed-supply registration obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping on every B2B invoice. VAT-registered vendors must issue full tax invoices, file VAT 201 returns electronically via eFiling, and submit payment linked to the SARS payslip reference. SARS operates data-driven e@sys validation, is progressively standardising e-invoicing through a SARS e-invoicing interoperability framework, and may require enhanced digital reporting for large taxpayers, but there is no per-invoice government clearance stamp.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act when they are physically exported from South Africa within the prescribed period and evidence of export is retained. Executive search/headhunting services supplied to a non-resident are zero-rated under section 11(2)(l) if the non-resident is not in South Africa at the time services are rendered and the services are not directly connected with immovable property or movable property situated in South Africa; the service supplier must retain the signed export service contract, proof of the foreign status and location of the client, and proof of payment in foreign currency. If the service is rendered to a South African resident or connected with a South African business, VAT must be charged at 15%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD500 container/air manifest, or SARS Customs export declaration)
Commercial invoice and VAT zero-rated export invoice
Bill of lading / air waybill / road or rail consignment note
Inward Foreign Exchange Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/MT202 bank credit advice evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Signed export or headhunting services contract establishing the foreign-resident status and place of supply of the client
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may deny zero-rating, raise additional VAT assessments, and impose interest for late payment. The Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 applies understatement penalties: 10% for a substantial understatement, 25% for failure to take reasonable care, 50% for a tax position with no reasonable grounds, 100% for an impermissible avoidance arrangement, and 150% for intentional tax evasion. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims may also attract criminal prosecution, retrospective clawback of VAT refunds, and debarment from future registration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933, with delegated administration to Authorised Dealers licensed under the exchange control regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is fully convertible for current-account transactions, including cross-border service fees, dividends, interest, and trade-related disbursements, subject to FIC Act reporting and supporting documentation; profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permissible through an Authorised Dealer provided the 20% Dividends Tax (DT) is withheld and the paying bank confirms the source of funds. Capital-account transactions, such as foreign equity subscription and offshore shareholder loans, remain controlled and require Authorised Dealer reporting to SARB FinSurv, with no general restriction for a low-risk executive search entity but with mandatory FDI reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For service exports under ISIC 7830 (executive search and headhunting), foreign-currency invoiced fees must be received in South Africa within 30 days from date of invoice and surrendered to an Authorised Dealer, or credited to a SARB-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA). There is no mandatory fixed conversion ratio; exporters may retain a portion in an FCA subject to Authorised Dealer limits and SARB directives, but onward repatriation, balances in excess of allowable thresholds, and any disposal require Authorised Dealer oversight. Statutory timeline: 30 days for both receipt and surrender/crediting to an FCA.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account plus Foreign Currency Account (FCA) for retainer wires and escrow of client funds

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: First National Bank (a division of FirstRand Bank Limited)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business Current Account / Operational Account with digital onboarding and dedicated FX desk
Corporate Current Account / Operational Account with Capital Escrow or trust overlay option
Corporate Account and Foreign Currency Account (FCA) for trade settlements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: MEDIUM for ancillary, small-ticket corridors only; not viable as the primary banking or escrow rail. Legal constraints: Wise B2B (Wise South Africa (Pty) Ltd) holds an FSCA financial-services provider licence and Authorised Dealer status but is not a deposit-taking bank; it cannot hold a corporate capital escrow or provide trust-level custody. ZAR clearing is routed via partner banks (e.g., Standard Bank), and high-value duplicate onboarding may trigger additional FICA documentation; therefore, the account structure should be Tier-1 led with fintech EMIs as a disbursement overlay.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For first account opening, directors must ordinarily complete a FICA-compliant identification process; physical presence is the default, but Tier-1 banks commonly accept remote onboarding where eFICA electronic verification succeeds for local directors. For non-resident directors, remote onboarding is acceptable with notarised/certified passport copies, apostilled corporate documents, a SARS tax clearance, and an independent beneficial-owner declaration; an in-person interview may be imposed only if the bank's AML profiling flags elevated risk. For this Low_Risk_Standard headhunting scope, physical presence can be waived with a notarised evidence pack, subject to final EDD discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO / beneficial-ownership opacity — nominee shareholding, offshore holding, or non-resident directors without a verifiable wealth trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Beneficial Owner Register per the FIC Act, corporate group diagram, certified passports/IDs of each natural person shareholder above 25% beneficial interest, statutory share register, and notarised source-of-wealth statements for all capital contributors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of SARS tax clearance or non-registration for income tax, VAT, or PAYE at account opening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid SARS Tax Compliance Status (Compliance Pin), company tax reference number, VAT registration certificate where turnover threshold met, PAYE/UIF registration proof, and a letter of good standing from an appointed tax practitioner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border retainer invoices flagged in sanctions or FX screening (sanctions-list hits, abnormally structured invoicing, or inconsistent counterparty profiles)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed headhunting retainer agreements, a full invoice trail aligned to the retainer schedule, UBO and sanctions screening reports for each counterparty, inward/outward FX purpose codes, and board resolutions approving each disbursement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of injected equity capital originating from unregulated or higher-risk offshore jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder bank statements covering the complete remittance chain, wealth-creation evidence (employment contracts, prior dividends, asset disposal agreements, inheritance/trust deeds), and an independent legal opinion or audit pack prepared by a SARB-recognised advisor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders subscribe for shares in the ZA_PTY_LTD entity via an Authorised Dealer (Tier-1 bank); remittance is executed by SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'FDI — share subscription', referencing the SARB FDI registration. The receiving bank credits a temporary capital suspense / escrow ledger, verifies the underlying subscription agreement and MOI, issues the share certificates, and files the inward foreign investment report with SARB FinSurv; only after the FDI reporting reference is captured may funds be swept into the operational ZAR account. Shareholder loans require an additional external-loan registration with the Authorised Dealer to secure future interest and principal remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for international retainer subscriptions (e.g., LinkedIn, contractor management platforms, software licences) are executed via SWIFT MT103 through the Authorised Dealer with prescribed purpose codes; larger procurement settlements may be structured using Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) or Documentary Collections, although direct telegraphic transfer is sufficient for ISIC 7830 services. For low-value recurring disbursements below the bank's threshold, Wise B2B can be used as an overlay rail; however, all disbursements must retain a clear audit trail and theatre purpose codes and remain within SARB current-account liberalisation limits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/ZAR FX forward contracts executed with an Authorised Dealer under an FX master agreement or ISDA
FX swaps (spot/forward combinations) for short-term working-capital liquidity management
Cross-currency swaps for foreign-currency shareholder-loan exposures, subject to bank credit approval and SARB reporting
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for onshore South African residents without explicit SARB FinSurv approval; onshore deliverable forwards remain the compliant alternative

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols require payment via SWIFT MT103 referencing purpose code FDI (Foreign Direct Investment) in favour of the company's Authorised Dealer bank, with escrowed proceeds credited to a Capital Escrow Account before conversion to ZAR. Verification includes the filed MOI, share subscription agreement, the FDI declaration form (or electronic FID reporting to SARB FinSurv), and proof of inward remittance from the overseas shareholder's bank for anti-money-laundering source-of-funds checks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements are executed primarily via SWIFT MT103 through the Authorised Dealer for retainer wires and vendor payments (LinkedIn subscriptions, contractor fees, and global research databases); large supplier payments may utilise Commercial Letters of Credit or Documentary Collections only where the headhunting commercial model requires them; for standard service disbursements the SWIFT relay plus Wise B2B overlay is the documented clearing rail with purpose codes retained for SARB reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/ZAR FX forward contracts with a licensed Authorised Dealer (on-shore)
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps with licensed banks for working-capital or trade-balance hedging
On-shore ZAR currency options for contract-proposal exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are restricted on-shore for residents; offshore NDF participation is impermissible under SARB exchange control without specific FinSurv approval and therefore excluded from the standard hedging toolkit

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the company's anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of ZAR 180 per overdue year; continued default for 1+ years triggers CIPC cancellation notice and administrative strike-off after final deregistration process.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) and Annual Financial Statements (for audit or independent review, as applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the financial year (unless SARS grants extension); provisional tax returns due on February and June half-yearly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS fixed non-compliance penalties up to ZAR 4,000 per month for late submission (depending on turnover); understatement penalty up to 200% of tax deficiency, plus interest at the repurchase rate plus 3.5%.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if Public Interest Score (PI) ≥ 350; independent review mandated if PI ≥ 100 but < 350; audits also required if the company is legally obliged to compile AFS under a regulatory mandate (e.g., FSCA licence) or if shareholders with ≥10% voting rights request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB, or IFRS for SMEs when eligible under the Companies Act (a private company with PI < 350 may apply IFRS for SMEs); full IFRS is mandatory for public interest scoring entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, before filing the annual return, the company must verify and update its beneficial ownership register and submit any changes to CIPC in the prescribed form. The annual return itself must confirm that the UBO register is complete and accurate; failure to maintain the register or file the confirmation is a criminal offence and may block annual return lodgement, leading to deregistration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (of shareholder and board meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No audit required for typical low-risk (Pty) Ltd with PI < 100; if triggered, certified audit estimate: $2,500 - $6,500; independent review estimate: $900 - $2,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (standard corporate income tax rate under section 5 of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, applicable to years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; the previous rate was 28%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No territorial tax holiday or generic export incentive is available for executive search services. Practical reductions: (1) Small Business Corporation (SBC) rates under section 12E for a (Pty) Ltd with gross income below ZAR 20 million and with all shareholders being natural persons: 0% up to ZAR 95,130, 7% from ZAR 95,131 to ZAR 364,000, 21% from ZAR 364,001 to ZAR 550,000, and 27% above ZAR 550,000 of taxable income. (2) Section 11D research and development deduction of 150% for qualifying scientific or technological R&D, potentially applicable to proprietary candidate-matching or AI-screening software. (3) Section 12H learnership allowances of up to ZAR 30,000 per annum per qualifying registered learner.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory carry-forward period for companies under section 20 of the Income Tax Act; utilisation is conditional on the continued carrying on of the same trade and on section 20A continuity-of-ownership tests where more than 50% of shareholding or voting rights change).
